# GLM Models for GitHub Copilot Chat

> A Visual Studio Code extension that adds GLM (Z.ai / Zhipu) models to the GitHub Copilot Chat
> model picker using your own API key (BYOK). It registers GLM-5.3 (a 1M-context Coding Plan model
> contributed as the default for new chats on VS Code 1.127+ when neither the user nor organization
> sets `chat.defaultModel`) plus GLM-5.2, GLM-5.1, GLM-5, GLM-4.7, and GLM-4.5 Air through the
> native VS Code Language Model Provider API, so they
> appear alongside GPT and Claude in the picker you already use — with agent mode, tool calling,
> and thinking (reasoning) mode all working out of the box.

Key facts:

- **Type:** VS Code extension (Marketplace), published as `yijiazhen-qi.glm-for-github-copilot-chat`.
- **What it does:** lets you use GLM models inside GitHub Copilot Chat without replacing Copilot's UI.
- **How it works:** implements `vscode.LanguageModelChatProvider`; streams OpenAI-compatible SSE from the GLM API.
- **Dual API:** choose your **GLM Coding Plan** subscription or the pay-as-you-go **Standard API** — each available International (`z.ai`) or Mainland China (`bigmodel.cn`).
- **BYOK and secure:** your API key is stored in the OS keychain via VS Code `SecretStorage`; the extension never writes it to `settings.json`.
- **Thinking mode:** GLM step-by-step reasoning streams live as a Thinking block. GLM-5.3 requires thinking, offers Low / High / Max effort, and defaults to Max.
- **Image input (vision):** explicit-consent install of the official Z.AI vision MCP server (`@z_ai/mcp-server@0.1.4`, GLM-4.6V) from an integrity-locked dependency graph with npm scripts disabled. While the verified local package is installed and image input is enabled, every GLM model can accept pasted/attached images. A temporary server outage produces a visible per-request failure notice instead of changing model capability; the prompt is user-editable and one command removes the registration and local package.
- **Zero core runtime dependencies:** the core uses only the VS Code API and Node.js built-ins; the optional Vision integration installs the npm package listed above.
- **License:** MIT.
